title: AdaptKit policy file (v0.1)
description: Everything the runtime needs to adapt a page: how to measure behaviour, how to turn it into a state, what to do in each state, and the safety rules. Produced by the Python trainer; read by any runtime.

is_placeholder.description: true = not trained on data yet (e.g. hand-written test values); must not be used in the study

trained_on.description: Plain description of the training data, e.g. 'simulated users calibrated on Findlater & Zhang (2020), train split'

window_size.description: How many recent selections the features look at

decision_every.description: A decision is made after every N-th selection

reference_fitts.description: Population Fitts' law model per device: predicted_ms = a_ms + b_ms_per_bit * ID

speed_ratio_cap.description: Speed ratios above this are treated as reading/deciding pauses and ignored (see features.md). Optional: no cap if absent.

bins.description: Ascending thresholds. value < t[0] -> 0; t[0] <= value < t[1] -> 1; ... A missing value maps to the middle bin (see features.md).

need_model.description: Logistic regression: need = sigmoid(intercept + sum(coef[f] * f)). Features: miss_rate, log_speed_ratio, variability, device_touch.

block_undone_actions.description: After the user undoes an action, that action is blocked for the rest of the session

table.description: State key -> action. State keys are built as described in features.md, e.g. 'm1-s2-v0-n2-t0-x0-c0-l0-d1'.

default_action.description: Used when a state is not in the table

q_values.description: Optional, for transparency: state key -> Q-value per action (same order as 'actions')
